
That error indicates there is no integration that can handle that `yaml` configuration.
You are probably missing an `(async_)setup` in `__init__.py`

I _think_ you need to call/trigger the import step manually, but I don't have actual experience with it. 

I suggest to look at  (closed) PRs for integrations that recently migrated from yaml to config_flow to see how it is done there.

> I think you need to call/trigger the import step manually, but I don't have actual experience with it.

Yes! Checkout `sensor.py` in `suez_water` for example. It still receives the YAML config like it does now, except it will now trigger a config flow init with the YAML as payload. If the import succeeded (or the import already was succesful) we create an issue to let the user know they can remove the YAML, if the import failed (because maybe the device can't be reached, credentials are incorrect, whatever) we raise a specific error telling the user what exactly went wrong. (Like, we don't want to just import everything and hope the user will make it work, if we can do our due dilligence and find out that the config entry won't work, we should raise an issue to let the user know what's up)

issue_context.title: Onkyo integration does not allow unique_id with individual configuration
issue_context.body:
### The problem

As far as I researched, the onkyo integration should already support unique_id. But for my configuration it seems not to be supported with an individual configuration. 
Or is it working as intended?



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.5.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

onkyo

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/onkyo/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
##spills an error
media_player:
  - platform: onkyo
    host: !secret id_onkyo
    name: Onkyo Living room
    unique_id: xxx-2797-yyy-ab48-zzz

## works and creates unique_id
media_player:
  - platform: onkyo
#    host: !secret id_onkyo
#    name: Onkyo Wohnzimmer
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Invalid config for 'onkyo' from integration 'media_player' at configuration.yaml, line 74: 'unique_id' is an invalid option for 'media_player.onkyo', check: unique_id
```


### Additional information

_No response_
comments: You don't define the unique id the integration does. Notice how that is not mentioned in the documentation?

Looks like only devices that are discovered by the integration get a unique ID, strange.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/onkyo/media_player.py#L263-L268

I agree, I felt the same already as I was writing it.

But as the library is not that well maintained currently, we cannot really change it.

For the longer term, I plan to rewrite and maintain a library myself. And then we can move all these consts and enums there.
I need to double check this with some others
iiirc use defined name. The model name comes from the device itself.

It depends on how the integration was setup.

If it was defined host, then name was declared there as well. If it was discovery, then the name was the same as model name, so nothing changes.

That said, after I added `unique_id` I don't think it is a problem. If some users are not happy with the name, they can always change it themselves. And if they already did, it is stored in the registry, so this doesn't have any impact.
Agree. Also, I think it's easier to recognize model name over hostname. Unless someone has two receivers of the same type, which seems like a very niche situation.
Maybe for the `async_step_user` you could return a menu, where you can ask "discovery" or "manual input". I think that increases usability
I borrowed this from the Wiz light integration I think. A menu would be nicer indeed.

Looking at this code, there seem to be some things missing/incorrect.

Was this tested? Does it actually work?
Fixed myself. Can be marked resolved.
